title: Console compact insight pathway - rebaseline scope and MVP cuts
creator: Nora Patel
description: PRD summary and scope-realignment note: We will ship a narrowed, production-safe surface for Console insights that delivers the highest ROI for reliability and cost transparency while deferring lower-value items. The intent of this ticket is to document concrete scope cuts, acceptance criteria, and a rollout guardrail for the compact insight pathway (single composite card + lightweight trace sampler + summary cost breakdown). This reduces telemetry ingestion and UI surface area to meet performance and shipping constraints for the April console release. Background: multiple stakeholders requested faster time-to-value for observability deliverables; engineering capacity and tokenization costs require trimming. This ticket captures the specific cuts, rationale, and rollout plan.
scope_changes: INCLUDE: Single composite insight card (route-level aggregates + 3 quick KPIs) replacing the planned 4 separate cards
INCLUDE: Lightweight trace sampler (event-based 1% steady-state sample, 10% burst window for incidents) rather than full distributed tracing UI in alpha
INCLUDE: Cost breakdown limited to top-5 routes by spend with hourly aggregation; exclude per-token cost drilldowns initially
EXCLUDE: Per-route timeline heatmaps and per-token breakdowns (deferred to follow-up epic)
EXCLUDE: Long-retention raw traces and full trace flamegraph explorer from MVP (deferred to Dedicated customers roadmap)
EXCLUDE: Custom card builder and ad-hoc query language in the first ship
decisions_log: 2026-01-14: PM + Eng sync - agreed to compress four insight cards into a single composite card to reduce front-end complexity and API surface (attendees: Nora, Ethan, Priya, Mateo). Reason: limited FE bandwidth and reduce telemetry ingestion by ~40%.
2026-01-20: Architecture review - agreed on event-based trace sampling with 1% baseline and a 10% incident window; kernel/ingest follow-up ENG-1984 to validate storage costs (lead: Mateo).
2026-01-25: UX review - simplified card accepted by Design with two micro-interactions for expand/collapse instead of a full drilldown. Design artifact link in Links section.

2026-02-02: Risk assessment - deferred per-token cost features because of high cardinality and SLA risks; mitigation: show top-5 routes only and add a 'request more detail' CTA for enterprise sales/SEs.
acceptance_criteria: Composite insight card renders under 300ms on median p95 path (measured on staging routes)
Trace sampler respects 1% baseline and 10% incident window; sampling metrics are emitted to telemetry (metric: console.trace.sample.rate)
Cost breakdown displays top-5 routes by spend with hourly rollup and matches billing data within 3% for the sampled window
UI: Expand/collapse interactions are accessible (keyboard + screen reader) and pass Design signoff (see design link)
Backend: API endpoints for composite card return summarized payloads and have pagination for >5 routes; response payload size < 50KB
OSS/Docs: Brief PRD update and runbook published to Confluence; release notes stub created in GH PR
Rollout: Canary at 5% of orgs then 25% with health checks (latency, error-rate, telemetry coverage) before 100% rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind 'insights.compact-pathway' - internal preview for SEs (start: 2026-02-22)
Phase 1: Canary - enable for 5% of orgs with low traffic; monitor telemetry for 72 hours
Phase 2: Ramp to 25% after passing health gates (latency < 1.3x baseline, error rate delta < 0.1%)
Phase 3: Full enablement after 7-day bake and final UX acceptance
notes: Design artifact includes microcopy variations; current UX copy selected to reduce cognitive load for customers unfamiliar with per-token economics.
Follow-up epic to reintroduce per-token cost drilldown is dependent on Dedicated storage optimization work (ENG-2022).
If sampling shows >10x variance in route-level spend estimates during canary, pause rollout and open ENG investigation.
PM action: schedule stakeholder demo with Sales/SEs the week after canary completion to capture field feedback.
